edges.description: Tick inoculation delivers organisms that then bind granulocyte receptors and enter neutrophils.
Receptor-dependent entry seeds the intracellular inclusion in which the bacterium can survive.
Intracellular organisms use a type IV secretion system to deliver AnkA into the host nucleus.
Intracellular organisms deliver Ats-1 to mitochondria and autophagy initiation machinery.
Intracellular Anaplasma remains dependent on its bacterial ribosome for protein synthesis.
Persistent intracellular organisms shuffle msp2(p44) pseudogenes to vary their major surface antigen.
Silencing CYBB suppresses the NADPH-oxidase component of neutrophil oxidative killing and helps intracellular organisms avoid bactericidal attack.
Blocking host-cell apoptosis and redirecting Beclin 1-dependent autophagy help infected cells remain permissive for intracellular bacterial growth.
Continual surface-antigen variation lets the organism escape the serotype-specific antibody response and persist.
Sustained infection elicits cytokine responses that converge on IFN-gamma-associated STAT1 signaling and inflammatory injury.
Replicating intracellular infection produces the characteristic acute febrile illness with leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and abnormal hepatic injury tests.
IFN-gamma-STAT1 signaling contributes to the immunopathologic inflammatory lesion arm of HGA.

nodes.description: The organism-level acute syndrome presents as an undifferentiated fever with cytopenias and biochemical liver injury; a minority of reported patients develop life-threatening complications such as ARDS or secondary HLH.

evidence.reference_title: Immune evasion and immunosuppression by Anaplasma phagocytophilum, the causative agent of tick-borne fever of ruminants and human granulocytic anaplasmosis.
evidence.snippet: Anaplasma phagocytophilum, the causative agent of tick-borne fever (TBF) in sheep and cattle and human granulocytic anaplasmosis, has the unique ability to infect and multiply within neutrophils, eosinophils and monocytes, cells at the frontline of the immune system.

nodes.description: The type IV secretion effector AnkA traffics into the granulocyte nucleus, binds AT-rich DNA at antimicrobial defense genes, recruits HDAC1 at the CYBB promoter, and represses NADPH oxidase expression, reducing respiratory-burst killing.

evidence.reference_title: Chromatin-bound bacterial effector ankyrin A recruits histone deacetylase 1 and modifies host gene expression.
evidence.snippet: Ankyrin A (AnkA), an A. phagocytophilum type IV secretion system effector, enters the granulocyte nucleus, binds stretches of AT-rich DNA and alters transcription of antimicrobial defence genes, including down-regulation of CYBB.

evidence.reference_title: Chromatin-bound bacterial effector ankyrin A recruits histone deacetylase 1 and modifies host gene expression.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, a direct interaction between AnkA and HDAC1 was detected at the CYBB promoter, and was critical for AnkA-mediated CYBB repression.

nodes.description: The A. phagocytophilum Ats-1 effector enters host mitochondria to suppress intrinsic apoptosis and also binds Beclin 1/Atg14L to nucleate autophagosomes that support the Anaplasma inclusion.

evidence.reference_title: Anaplasma phagocytophilum Ats-1 is imported into host cell mitochondria and interferes with apoptosis induction.
evidence.snippet: Ats-1 inhibited etoposide-induced cytochrome c release from mitochondria, PARP cleavage, and apoptosis in mammalian cells, as well as Bax-induced yeast apoptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Autophagosomes induced by a bacterial Beclin 1 binding protein facilitate obligatory intracellular infection.
evidence.snippet: Thus, Anaplasma actively induces autophagy by secreting Ats-1 that hijacks the Beclin 1-Atg14L autophagy initiation pathway likely to acquire host nutrients for its growth.

nodes.description: Because A. phagocytophilum replicates inside granulocytes, treatment must use agents that achieve intracellular concentrations rather than poorly cell-penetrant antibiotics.

evidence.reference_title: Intracellular Pharmacokinetics of Antibacterials and Their Clinical Implications.
evidence.snippet: Therapeutic efficacy against intracellular pathogens has been correlated mainly with the intracellular concentrations achieved by the different antimicrobial agents.
